findings.summary: V1's mandated evidence mechanism is absent: no test ever drives production spawnAnchorCheck through a real subprocess. The whole G14 file mocks node:child_process.execFileSync and hand-fabricates the failure object via makeExecError (err.status / err.stdout / err.stderr), while ANCHOR_CHECK_BIN is set to the nonexistent "/fake/anchor-check", so real execFileSync is never invoked. The defect under repair IS the mismatch between production's assumption about execFileSync's non-zero-exit error contract and Node's actual behavior; a test that synthesizes exactly the fields the implementation reads cannot fail if that assumption were wrong (e.g. reading e.output[1] or a Buffer-vs-string field would still pass). Spec V1 requires "用一个假二进制（shell 脚本：打印固定 JSON 后 exit 1）驱动生产 spawnAnchorCheck；⛔ 这是本包的存在理由", and spec §4 states the dispatcher already proved this satisfiable with a few-line shell fake needing no network or real corpus. The mechanism is also demonstrably available in this repo (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:746-753 and test/tick-run.test.ts:743-744 write real bash stubs with chmodSync 0o755). V1-V9 are 缺一不可.

The V8 reachability declaration closes with a false evidence claim: "V6 验证 assembleGenerateDeps 产出的 spawnAnchorCheck 经真实 execFileSync". In test/g14-anchor-exit-code.test.ts, execFileSync is mocked file-wide (lines 29-40, passing through only cmd === "git"), and every V1/V3/V4/V5/V6 case sets ANCHOR_CHECK_BIN to "/fake/anchor-check"; no case in that file reaches the real execFileSync. Spec §4 explicitly forbids asserting evidence that was not actually obtained.

The loud-failure branch discards the diagnosis for two of the three cases V4 names. When e.status is null (timeout kill, missing binary/ENOENT), exitCode becomes the literal "killed" and stderrTail is "" because e.stderr is undefined, and the original error message (e.g. "spawnSync /path ENOENT") is dropped, never included. The resulting report head reads "dr-anchor-rate unavailable anchor-check-failed:anchor-check killed:" with no cause, defeating spec §1's requirement that unavailable's 成因 be diagnosable on the report head and V4's requirement to 点名退出码与 stderr 尾部 for the 超时 / 二进制缺失 / 真崩溃 cases. No test covers either case.

Exit code 0 with non-JSON stdout is misreported as "killed". JSON.parse(stdout) on the success path throws a SyntaxError that falls into the same catch; that error has no .status, .stdout or .stderr, so the thrown message is "anchor-check killed: " even though the process exited 0 and was not killed. V4 requires the error to name the exit code for every non-parseable-stdout case.

The failure message is interpolated into the report head's HTML comment without sanitization: anchorTail = `anchor-check-failed:${msg}` embeds up to 200 chars of raw stderr, which for a real anchor-check crash is a multi-line Python traceback and may contain "-->". renderReportHead emits `<!-- dr-anchor-rate ${rate} -->` on one line, so the head marker line can be split across lines or terminated early, corrupting the single-line head contract that the export path and downstream readers depend on.

The three explicit V6 cases are tautological and carry no evidence: each rebuilds deps from assembleGenerateDeps and then asserts only expect(deps.spawnAnchorCheck).toBeDefined() and typeof === "function", never calling it. They pass against any implementation, including the unfixed one. V6's substance rides entirely on the V1/V3/V4 cases, which are themselves undermined by the blocker above.
